description:
A profile package is constructed from a directory tree, owning the bytes it validates, so a package that is not compiled into the binary can exist at all.

## Background

The package model was written as if its bytes were untrusted external data, and almost all of it already holds for a package of unknown provenance: it takes a path-to-bytes map, bounds file count and total size, rejects absolute, traversal, Windows-prefix, control-character and backslash paths, rejects a declared source that is absent and a package file no declaration claims, rejects duplicate sources and duplicate targets, and content-addresses the manifest and every path.

Two things stand in the way. The only constructor that exists walks a directory compiled in at build time. And the type borrows the byte slices it validates, which a disk read cannot supply without leaking them. A directory walk producing a path-to-bytes map, over a representation that can own its bytes, is therefore the entire new reader.

What the reader must not do is relax any defence. A package read from a working tree is exactly the untrusted input those bounds were written for, and a directory entry that is not a regular file, or a path that escapes the package root, has to be rejected where the package is read rather than where its content is used.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A profile package is constructed from a directory path, owning the bytes it validates.
- [hard] REQ-02: For the same content, a directory-read package and a compile-time package are equal in manifest, package hash, and per-target digests.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every existing package defence applies to a directory-read package: the file-count and total-size bounds, the rejected path shapes, the absent declared source, and the undeclared package file.
- [hard] REQ-04: A directory entry that is not a regular file, and any path escaping the package root, is rejected with a message naming it.
- [hard] REQ-05: A directory that is absent or unreadable is reported as such rather than as an invalid package.

## Notes

Where a package directory comes from is decided elsewhere. This is the reader alone.
title: Read a profile package from a directory on disk
